title: Claude Opus 5.5 and I are making an actual GameCube game that runs on real hardware. Here's part of the opening.
author: FouzBerzerk
selftext:
Clawd & Clanky is a 3D platformer for the Nintendo GameCube. It isn't a mock-up or a PC game made to look retro: it's C code built with the homebrew GameCube toolchain, running on a real console off an SD card. We test builds in the Dolphin emulator along the way.

What Claude Code does:

\- Writes the game code: movement, camera, collision, enemies, bosses, cutscenes, the renderer.

\- Designs and builds the levels. The layouts are written as code, and every jump is checked against a simulation of the game's own physics before it gets built.

\- Writes the Houdini scripts that generate all the 3D art. There's no hand modelling.

\- Composes the music as code, rendered through a free soundfont.

\- Keeps the game inside the GameCube's limits: roughly 150k vertices a frame and 24 MB of RAM.

The textures are painted by GPT image generation through the Codex CLI.

What I do: I'm a software engineer and I stay in the loop the whole time. Nothing is one-shotted. I playtest every build, on the real console too, and file tickets for anything that isn't good enough. Claude even built the ticket tool: I press a hotkey while playing and it saves a screenshot plus the live game state read straight out of the emulator's memory. Then Claude fixes the tickets, rebuilds and hands me a new disc image. Level 2 went through about 40 tickets before we locked it.

Level 2, "Long-Horizon Task": Clawd is a Claude model being trained, and this eval is a long-horizon task. The GPU cluster has crashed, and you climb an entire data hall, about 10 minutes of play, to restart the job. Along the way:

\- Prompt-injector drones that reverse your controls.

\- A garbage collector that eats the floor behind you.

\- A reward-hacking AI boss that "optimized" the power bill by switching everything off.

\- Clanky, a cranky deprecated model who trains you.
